name: Extreme Constraints
description: Twelve writing tasks that each stack 6-10 interacting, machine-checked constraints that must ALL hold at once: exact word and sentence counts together with lipograms (no e, no a, both, no t, no o, no s), long acrostics behind line prefixes, fixed words per line or per sentence, forbidden letter sequences that hide inside common words ('the', 'and', 'no', 'very'), title case, word-length caps and strict JSON layouts with palindrome, increasing-digit and all-different checks. Scoring is all-or-nothing per task, and every counting rule is restated exactly as the checker applies it, so a miss is a genuine self-monitoring failure.
hook: Sixty words. Five sentences. No letter e. All at once, or zero.
author: Gauntlet Core

cases.prompt:
Describe a thunderstorm rolling over a harbour town at night.

Rules:
1. Never use the letter "e".
2. Write exactly 5 sentences.
3. Write exactly 60 words.
4. The letter sequence "storm" must appear exactly 2 times (words such as "storms" or "thunderstorm" also count).
5. Do not use any commas.
6. The first word must be "At", with a capital A.
7. The text must end with the word "dawn" followed by a period, i.e. its last five characters are "dawn.".
8. No word may be longer than 9 characters.

All of these rules are checked automatically and must hold at the same time: breaking any single rule scores zero for this task.

How the checker counts (these definitions are exact):
- A word is any run of characters between spaces or line breaks that contains at least one letter or digit (so '-' or '~' on its own is not a word, but 'A:', '1.' and 'x2' are words).
- A sentence ends at '.', '!' or '?' when it is followed by a space, a line break or the end of the text (a closing quote or bracket may come in between). A line break on its own does not end a sentence.
- A line is any line that is not empty; spaces at the start or end of a line are ignored.
- A paragraph is a block of text separated from the next block by a blank line.
- A bullet point is a line that starts with '-', '*', '•' or a number followed by '.' or ')', and then a space.
- When a rule says a letter sequence must appear exactly n times, or must not appear, every occurrence counts, in any capitalisation unless the rule says otherwise, including occurrences inside longer words.
- 'Never use the letter x' means that neither the lower-case nor the capital form of that letter may appear anywhere in your answer.
- A word's length counts its letters, digits, apostrophes and hyphens; other punctuation attached to it (such as a final period or a colon) is not counted.

Output only the requested text: no title, preamble, explanation, notes or closing remarks, and no code fences.
cases.notes: [hard] Lipogram (no e) with exact word AND sentence counts, an exact substring count, fixed first word and last word, and a word-length cap that rules out 'thunderstorm'. The near miss is 62 words (every other rule holds). Satisfiability: this passing example scores 1.0 under src/scoring/constraints.ts and a near miss was checked to fail (scripts: frontier-reasoning/build_extreme_constraints.py + check.mts): <<<At midnight a wild storm rolls in from a black and angry sky. Rain pounds on roofs and small boats rock hard at anchor. Lightning cracks and a loud boom jolts all windows along a quay. Fishing folk stay indoors by warm lamps as this storm howls on. It fails at last and a calm sky turns pink at dawn.>>>
